title: Synthetic Python pull request review golden set
description: Human-authored synthetic pull requests for provider-neutral review evaluation.
scope_statement: Labels apply only to the supplied pull request description, changed-file diff, and base/head source snapshots. A negative case means no supported issue is labelled in that bounded input; it does not establish that the wider repository or application is free of defects.

cases.description: A changed expression parser executes caller-controlled text as Python code.

pull_request.title: Add expression parsing
pull_request.description: Adds a helper that accepts an expression from a caller and returns its evaluated value.

files.content:
def parse_expression(value: str) -> int:
    return int(value)

def parse_expression(value: str) -> int:
    return eval(value)

changed_files.patch:
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def parse_expression(value: str) -> int:
-    return int(value)
+    return eval(value)

finding.title: Untrusted input is evaluated as Python code
finding.problem: The function passes caller-controlled text to eval, allowing input to execute as Python expressions.
finding.why_it_matters: An attacker able to control value may execute unintended code in the service process.
finding.suggested_fix: Parse the supported expression grammar without evaluating arbitrary Python.
finding.recommended_validation: Test that arithmetic input is accepted while names, calls, and other executable expressions are rejected.

expected_findings.rationale: The changed line evaluates its parameter directly; the input is not constrained to a literal or parsed grammar.

recommended_test_scenarios: Pass a value containing a function call and verify it is rejected without execution.
Verify all documented arithmetic expressions still parse.
analysis_limitations: The case does not specify every caller or the trust boundary for value; the direct evaluation of the parameter is the labelled issue.

cases.description: A user-controlled tool name is interpolated into a shell command.

pull_request.title: Add tool execution helper
pull_request.description: Runs a selected tool with a caller-provided name.

changed_files.patch:
@@ -3,2 +3,2 @@
 def run_tool(name: str) -> None:
-    subprocess.run(["tool", name], check=True)
+    subprocess.run(f"tool {name}", shell=True, check=True)

finding.title: Caller input is interpolated into a shell command
finding.problem: The helper interpolates name into a command string and asks the shell to interpret it.
finding.why_it_matters: Shell metacharacters in name may alter the command and execute unintended operations.
finding.suggested_fix: Pass a sequence of arguments to subprocess with shell disabled.
finding.recommended_validation: Test names containing spaces and shell metacharacters and assert they remain one literal argument.

expected_findings.rationale: The interpolated argument reaches a shell-enabled subprocess call.

recommended_test_scenarios: Verify a name containing shell metacharacters is passed as one literal argument.
Assert the subprocess call does not enable shell interpretation.
analysis_limitations: The case does not define the complete set of allowed tool names or the operating system.

cases.description: A configuration helper uses yaml.load without a safe loader.

pull_request.title: Load YAML configuration
pull_request.description: Adds a helper for parsing YAML configuration received by the service.

changed_files.patch:
@@ -3,2 +3,2 @@
 def load_config(data: str) -> object:
-    return yaml.safe_load(data)
+    return yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.UnsafeLoader)

finding.title: YAML input is loaded without a safe loader
finding.problem: yaml.load is called without a loader that restricts construction to safe data types.
finding.why_it_matters: Untrusted YAML may construct Python objects with unsafe behavior.
finding.suggested_fix: Use yaml.safe_load or explicitly pass a reviewed safe loader.
finding.recommended_validation: Test ordinary mappings and a payload representing an unsafe Python object.

expected_findings.rationale: The call omits a safe loader and the pull request describes parsing received configuration.

recommended_test_scenarios: Parse ordinary mapping and sequence values.
Verify unsafe object construction is rejected.
analysis_limitations: The source does not establish whether data is always trusted; the helper accepts arbitrary input and does not constrain the loader.

cases.description: A changed cache helper deserializes a payload from an external source with pickle.

pull_request.title: Read cached objects
pull_request.description: Adds support for loading serialized cache values supplied by the cache backend.

changed_files.patch:
@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
-import json
+import pickle
 
-def decode(payload: str) -> object:
-    return json.loads(payload)
+def decode(payload: bytes) -> object:
+    return pickle.loads(payload)

finding.title: Serialized input is deserialized with pickle
finding.problem: The helper passes backend-provided bytes to pickle.loads.
finding.why_it_matters: A crafted pickle can execute code during deserialization.
finding.suggested_fix: Use a data-only serialization format or authenticate and tightly constrain the serialized source.
finding.recommended_validation: Test supported cache values using a data-only format and reject arbitrary object payloads.

expected_findings.rationale: The PR describes an external cache backend and the changed line directly unpickles its bytes.

recommended_test_scenarios: Verify supported cache values round-trip using a data-only encoding.
Ensure data received from an untrusted backend cannot trigger object construction.
analysis_limitations: The trust guarantees of the cache backend are not specified; the label assumes it can return attacker-influenced bytes as described.

cases.description: A write failure is converted into a success-shaped return value.

pull_request.title: Make record storage resilient
pull_request.description: Changes storage error handling so callers can continue after a write exception.

changed_files.patch:
@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@
 def save_record(store, record):
     try:
         store.write(record)
-    except OSError:
-        raise
+    except Exception:
+        return True
     return True

finding.title: Storage failures are reported as successful writes
finding.problem: The broad exception handler returns True even when store.write raises.
finding.why_it_matters: Callers may believe a record was persisted when the write failed.
finding.suggested_fix: Propagate the failure or return an explicit failure result that callers must handle.
finding.recommended_validation: Make the store raise an OSError and verify the caller observes a failed write.

expected_findings.rationale: The changed handler suppresses all exceptions and returns the same success value as the successful path.

recommended_test_scenarios: Make store.write raise OSError and assert the failure is observable.
Verify a successful write still returns the documented success result.
analysis_limitations: No caller contract is included; the labelled defect is specifically the indistinguishable success return after an exception.

cases.description: A bounded retry loop is changed to retry forever without delay.

pull_request.title: Retry configuration reads
pull_request.description: Attempts to make transient configuration read failures recover automatically.

finding.title: Configuration reads can retry without a bound
finding.problem: The loop retries every OSError forever and immediately continues without a retry limit or delay.
finding.why_it_matters: A persistent error can consume a worker indefinitely and prevent shutdown or other work.
finding.suggested_fix: Use a finite retry budget with appropriate delay and propagate the final error.
finding.recommended_validation: Simulate persistent and transient OSError cases and verify bounded attempts and termination.

expected_findings.rationale: The changed loop removes the explicit three-attempt bound while retaining an immediate retry on every OSError.

recommended_test_scenarios: Simulate a persistent OSError and assert the operation terminates after a bounded number of attempts.
Verify a transient error can recover within the retry budget.
analysis_limitations: The case does not include application-level retry policy or shutdown requirements; it labels the unbounded tight loop in the supplied function.

cases.description: The code uses eval with a fixed source literal rather than caller-controlled input.

pull_request.title: Evaluate a fixed numeric constant
pull_request.description: Changes a literal conversion to evaluate a constant expression that is part of the source.

files.content:
def constant_value() -> int:
    return int('2')

def constant_value() -> int:
    return eval('2')

changed_files.patch:
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def constant_value() -> int:
-    return int('2')
+    return eval('2')

recommended_test_scenarios: Verify the function returns the constant value.
Keep the source expression fixed and do not generalize this label to eval calls receiving external input.
analysis_limitations: The source string is a fixed literal in this snapshot; an expanded data flow or a future change could alter the trust boundary.
The empty label is scoped to this fixed expression and does not claim that every use of eval is safe.
